subtopic: Kossel and Lewis Approach to Chemical Bonding
stem: Write Lewis structure of nitrite ion \(\mathrm{NO_2^{\ominus}}\).
solution:
**Step I :** Count the total number of valence electrons of nitrogen atom, oxygen atom and one electron of additional negative charge.

\(\mathrm{N}(2s^2 2p^3)\), \(\mathrm{O}\ (2s^2 2p^4)\)

\(5 + (2 \times 6) + 1 = 18\) electrons

**Step II :** The skeletal structure of \(\mathrm{NO_2^{\ominus}}\) is written as \(\mathrm{O\ N\ O}\)

**Step III :** Draw a single bond i.e. one shared electron pair between the nitrogen and each oxygen atoms completing the octet on oxygen atom. This does not complete the octet of nitrogen. Hence, there is a multiple bond between nitrogen and one of the oxygen atoms (a double bond). The remaining two electrons constitute a lone pair on nitrogen.

Following are Lewis dot structures of \(\mathrm{NO_2^{\ominus}}\).

\(\left[:\!\overset{\bullet\bullet}{\underset{\bullet\bullet}{\mathrm{O}}}\!:\!\underset{\bullet\bullet}{\mathrm{N}}\!:\!\overset{\bullet\bullet}{\underset{\bullet\bullet}{\mathrm{O}}}\!:\right]^{\ominus}\)

\(\left[\overset{\bullet\bullet}{\underset{\bullet\bullet}{\mathrm{O}}} = \overset{\bullet\bullet}{\mathrm{N}} - \overset{\bullet\bullet}{\underset{\bullet\bullet}{\mathrm{O}}}\!:\right]^{\ominus}\) or \(\left[:\!\overset{\bullet\bullet}{\underset{\bullet\bullet}{\mathrm{O}}} - \overset{\bullet\bullet}{\mathrm{N}} = \overset{\bullet\bullet}{\underset{\bullet\bullet}{\mathrm{O}}}\right]^{\ominus}\)
_note: p-03 (printed p.58), right column. The book prints `Solution` with NO colon here — the only worked example in the chapter that does. The three closing dot structures are drawn inline; the linear rendering above preserves the bonding (2 single bonds in the first, one double bond in each resonance form) and the electron count of 18, but the exact vertical placement of each lone pair on the printed page cannot be reproduced losslessly in linear notation.

subtopic: Kossel and Lewis Approach to Chemical Bonding
stem: Write the Lewis structure of \(\mathrm{CO}\) molecule.
solution:
**Step - I .** Count number of electrons of carbon and oxygen atoms. The valence shell configuration of carbon and oxygen atoms are : \(2s^2 2p^2\) and \(2s^2 2p^4\) respectively. The valence electrons available are

\(4 + 6 = 10\)

**Step - II :** The skeletal structure of \(\mathrm{CO}\) is written as

\(:\!\mathrm{C}\!:\!\ddot{\mathrm{O}}\!:\) or \(:\!\mathrm{C}-\ddot{\mathrm{O}}\!:\)

**Step - III :** Draw a single bond (One shared electron pair) between C and O and complete the octet on O. The remaining two electrons is a lone pair on C.

The octet on carbon is not complete hence there is a multiple bond between C and O (a triple bond between C and O atom). This satisfies the octet rule for carbon and oxygen atoms.

\(:\!\mathrm{C} \equiv \mathrm{O}\!:\)
_note: p-04 (printed p.59), left column. Carries a line-start `Solution :` label. The book also prints an overlapping-circles pictorial of the same structure beside the linear form; it adds nothing the linear form does not carry, so it is not cropped.

subtopic: Kossel and Lewis Approach to Chemical Bonding
stem:
Find out the formal charges on S, C, N.

\((\mathrm{S} = \mathrm{C} = \mathrm{N})^{\ominus}\) ; \((\mathrm{S} - \mathrm{C} \equiv \mathrm{N})^{\ominus}\); \((\mathrm{S} \equiv \mathrm{C} - \mathrm{N})^{\ominus}\)
solution:
**Step I**

Write Lewis dot diagrams for the structure

\(\overset{\bullet\bullet}{\underset{\bullet\bullet}{\mathrm{S}}} = \mathrm{C} = \overset{\bullet\bullet}{\underset{\bullet\bullet}{\mathrm{N}}}\)  (A)   \(:\!\overset{\bullet\bullet}{\underset{\bullet\bullet}{\mathrm{S}}} - \mathrm{C} \equiv \mathrm{N}\!:\)  (B)   \(:\!\mathrm{S} \equiv \mathrm{C} - \overset{\bullet\bullet}{\underset{\bullet\bullet}{\mathrm{N}}}\!:\)  (C)

**Step II**

Assign formal charges

\(\mathrm{FC} = \mathrm{V.E} - \mathrm{N.E} - \tfrac{1}{2}\,\mathrm{B.E.}\)

**Structure A :**

Formal charge on \(\mathrm{S} = 6 - 4 - \tfrac{1}{2}(4) = 0\)

Formal charge on \(\mathrm{C} = 4 - 0 - \tfrac{1}{2}(8) = 0\)

Formal charge on \(\mathrm{N} = 5 - 4 - \tfrac{1}{2}(4) = -1\)

**Structure B :**

Formal charge on \(\mathrm{S} = 6 - 6 - \tfrac{1}{2}(2) = -1\)

Formal charge on \(\mathrm{C} = 4 - 0 - \tfrac{1}{2}(8) = 0\)

Formal charge on \(\mathrm{N} = 5 - 2 - \tfrac{1}{2}(6) = 0\)

**Structure C :**

Formal charge on \(\mathrm{S} = 6 - 2 - \tfrac{1}{2}(6) = +1\)

Formal charge on \(\mathrm{C} = 4 - 0 - \tfrac{1}{2}(8) = 0\)

Formal charge on \(\mathrm{N} = 5 - 6 - \tfrac{1}{2}(2) = -2\)
_note: p-05 (printed p.60), right column. Carries a line-start `Solution :` label. Checked: every one of the nine formal charges evaluates as printed, and each structure's charges sum to -1, matching the ion's charge — no defect.

solution:
Electronic configuration of berylium

| | 1s | 2s | 2p |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ground state | \(\uparrow\downarrow\) | \(\uparrow\downarrow\) | — — — |
| Excited state | \(\uparrow\downarrow\) | \(\uparrow\) | \(\uparrow\) — — |
| sp Hybridized | \(\uparrow\downarrow\) | \(\uparrow\ \uparrow\) (two sp hybrid orbitals) | — — (pure 'p' orbitals) |

**Formation of \(\mathrm{BeCl_2}\) molecule.**

This molecule has one Be atom and two chlorine atoms. Electronic configuration of Be is \(\mathrm{1s^2,\ 2s^2,\ 2p_z^0}\). The 2s and \(\mathrm{2p_z}\) orbitals undergo sp hybridization to form two sp hybrid orbitals oriented at \(180^\circ\) with each other. \(\mathrm{2p_z}\) orbitals of two chlorine atoms overlap with the sp hybrid orbitals to form two sp-p \(\sigma\) bond.
_note: p-15 (printed p.70), left column. This worked example carries NO `Solution` label of any kind — the heading line is `Problem 5.4 / Explain the formation of BeCl2` and the working begins immediately with the electronic configuration. The book's orbital-box diagram is transcribed as the table above (its two sp orbitals are drawn in the 2s column and the two remaining pure p boxes in the 2p column, which the table preserves). The accompanying orbital-overlap drawing is illustrative of the prose that follows it and is not cropped.
